## 1. New LLM Versions / Major AI Lab Tools
- Date: `2026-04-22`
  Link: [Introducing workspace agents in ChatGPT](https://openai.com/index/introducing-workspace-agents-in-chatgpt)
  Summary: OpenAI introduced Codex-powered workspace agents in ChatGPT that run in the cloud, connect to tools, and automate repeatable workflows for teams.
  Why it matters: This is a concrete move from chat assistance toward delegated, tool-using execution inside OpenAI’s main product.

- Date: `2026-04-22`
  Link: [Speeding up agentic workflows with WebSockets in the Responses API](https://openai.com/index/speeding-up-agentic-workflows-with-websockets)
  Summary: OpenAI published a WebSockets-based pattern for Responses API agent loops, using connection-scoped caching to reduce overhead and latency.
  Why it matters: It gives builders an official low-latency architecture for production agent systems, not just a model endpoint.

## 2. FOSS / Open-Weight LMs & Tools
- Date: `2026-04-22`
  Link: [Introducing OpenAI Privacy Filter](https://openai.com/index/introducing-openai-privacy-filter)
  Summary: OpenAI released Privacy Filter, an open-weight model for detecting and redacting personally identifiable information in text.
  Why it matters: It provides a deployable privacy-control component for enterprise pipelines that cannot rely only on closed APIs.

  Link: [Qwen3.6-27B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B) and [Qwen3.6-35B-A3B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B)
  Summary: Qwen published two first Qwen3.6 open-weight variants on Hugging Face: a 27B dense model and a 35B-A3B MoE model.
